newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish SOP sees end-Jan pulp derivatives launch.
newsitem.headline: Finnish SOP sees end-Jan pulp derivatives launch.

text.p: Finnish options exchange Suomen Optioporssi (SOP) will start trade in pulp derivatives at the end of January, about four months behind schedule, SOP managing director Anders Lindeberg said on Tuesday.

It had not yet been cleared who would participate in the trade and this had delayed the launch. The number of traders now looked set to rise to between 20 and 30, enough for initial trade, Lindeberg said.
"We are now just going through the final little things ... we are looking to start at the end of January," he told Reuters by telephone.

It is likely that Finnish brokerage houses will not be able to take part from the start due to a law that excludes commodities from the list of instruments they can trade. This law may be altered later, Lindeberg said.

SOP's pulp options and futures -- which treat pulp as a commodity based on SOP's own pulp price benchmark index -- can be used by the forest industry and buyers to hedge against pulp price fluctuations.
